metadata.note: Chesapeake Western (Virginia): Elkton - Harrisonburg - Bridgewater - Stokesville - North River Gap short line, opened 1896 to Bridgewater and 1902-1904 to Stokesville and North River Gap. Chartered 1892 as the Chesapeake, Shenandoah and Western; built 1895-96 as the Chesapeake and Western Railroad; renamed Tidewater and West Virginia 1900; leased 1901 to the Chesapeake Western Railway 'with the same management'. One enterprise throughout the drawn years, so no Rule 4 split; W.E.D. Stokes / estate / D.W. Thomas (1938) stock changes are not operator changes, and the N&W purchase (1954) came after passenger service had ended. The Elkton junction is with the N&W Shenandoah Valley line (OSM relation 8840808, see research/notes/osm-nw-virginia-districts.md). Built from research/branches/chesapeake_western_railway.txt (researched 2026-10-27).
sources: Fowler, branchline.uk Virginia Railroads SL 225, table 83 (mileposts)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), fetched 2026-10-27 and routed with opstrace.py, Operator 'Chesapeake Western': every mile follows OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=Chesapeake Western - the active Norfolk Southern track named 'Chesapeake Western' (Elkton - Harrisonburg - Pleasant Hill area) and railway=abandoned grade ways beyond it, some of them residential roads built on the grade (Chesapeake Lane, Old C and W Railroad Road, Stokesville Road). OpenHistoricalMap was queried over Bridgewater - North River Gap and returned no railway ways. The CW-tagged 'Shenandoah Valley Railroad' track (ex-B&O Harrisonburg - Staunton, CW only from 1943) is not used.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] ends on every feature: Elkton - Harrisonburg 1937 (bracket 1937-1951; 1937 forum claim vs 'late 1940s' caption, unresolved), Harrisonburg - Bridgewater 1911 (bracket 1911-1951; 1921 likely but unproven), Bridgewater - Stokesville 1911 (bracket 1911-1930; 1916 resort ad indirect), Stokesville - North River Gap 1911 (and its 1904 start is earliest-confirmed, [OPEN]). Best next sources: CW ICC annual reports, Virginia SCC discontinuance order, Harrisonburg Daily News-Record 'last train' story, JMU Special Collections CW records 1928-1982. (2) Opening date 23 Mar vs late Apr 1896. (3) All headway_min values are estimates from timetable train counts or guesses; avg_speed_kmh is a guess. (4) Station sites at Harrisonburg, Bridgewater and North River Gap not established. (5) Whether the CW carried passengers on the ex-B&O Harrisonburg - Staunton line after 1943 - no evidence either way.
metadata.omissions: NOT DRAWN: (a) Harrisonburg - Staunton (ex-B&O Valley Railroad, CW from 1 Jan 1943) - no confirmable CW passenger year; the Feb 1952 Guide's Elkton - Staunton table reads 'Freight, Mail and Express only' (Rule 1); its B&O passenger history belongs to the B&O. (b) Staunton - Lexington, bought 1943 and soon abandoned - no CW passenger service. (c) The 1902 Stokesville logging tramway toward Wooddell Springs - industrial, not public passenger service. (d) Every CW line after its passenger end: freight continued (Rule 1).

LATER ALIGNMENT: this is the present-day NS track; no realignment since 1896 is known, but none was checked against an early map, so minor curve or yard changes (Elkton junction, Harrisonburg) may be drawn on their modern form. The Harrisonburg end point is a split vertex 1.3 km from the city-centre geocode; the CW station site is not established. Simplified Douglas-Peucker 8 m.

segments.note: Opened for public traffic April 1896 (company invitation, Richmond Times 28 Apr 1896; first public schedule effective 29 Apr 1896, Staunton Vindicator 15 May 1896). CONFLICT recorded: Wikipedia / american-rails give official opening 23 Mar 1896; the year is 1896 either way. Operated by the Chesapeake and Western Railroad (renamed Tidewater and West Virginia 1900), leased from 1901 to the Chesapeake Western Railway under the same management - one enterprise, no Rule 4 split. The 1896 table shows 2 trains each way (Mixed No. 20 and Express No. 2 east, Express No. 1 and Mixed No. 19 west, Bridgewater - Elkton); headway_min 480 is an estimate from that count. Train counts for 1897-1903 were not checked and the 1896 figure is carried forward.
sources: Segment-level: Richmond Times 1896-04-28 p5 (opening invitation); Staunton Vindicator 1896-05-15 p2 (schedule eff. 29 Apr 1896). Headway estimated from the 1896 train count.

segments.note: Staunton Spectator timetables 1904-1911 show 3 trains each way (Nos. 2/4/6 east, 3/5/19 west), connecting with the N&W at Elkton and the B&O Valley RR / Southern at Harrisonburg. headway_min 360 is an estimate from that count. 1912-1920 carries the line forward between the 1911 timetable and the 1921 stories below, which show passenger trains still running; no timetable for 1912-1920 was seen.
sources: Segment-level: Staunton Spectator timetables 1904-06-10 p4, 1907-07-12 p4, 1911-03-10 p1. 1912-1920 not individually sourced - continuity between the 1911 timetable and the 1921 newspaper evidence.

segments.note: Feb 1921 the road applied to the State Corporation Commission to discontinue all passenger trains; local citizens got the hearing postponed (Washington Herald 12 Feb 1921). Mar 1921 it was experimenting with motor-driven cars (Washington Herald 13 Mar 1921), and by Sep 1921 a gasoline 'passenger street car' seating ~24 that stopped anywhere on the line was in service (Brattleboro Daily Reformer 21 Sep 1921). Last positive evidence: an Oct 1937 photograph of 4-4-0 #102 with a passenger train at the Elkton passenger station (rrpicturearchives). headway_min 720 is a guess - no 1921-1937 frequency was found. CONFLICT recorded: a railroadfan.com forum post (search summary only) says passenger service ended and equipment was scrapped in 1937; an rrpicturearchives caption says passenger business 'dried up completely ... in the late 1940's' (hedged, inferred from motor car M-75 bought Dec 1941). The Feb 1952 Official Guide shows the CW Elkton - Staunton table 'Operates for Freight, Mail and Express only', so service was gone by 1951. Freight continues under Norfolk Southern (context only). [OPEN] 1937 is the last CONFIRMED year of passenger service on this stretch, not a known end - no source dates when passenger trains actually stopped here. Do not extend without evidence. The end bracket is 1937-1951.
sources: Segment-level: Washington Herald 1921-02-12 p3 and 1921-03-13 p5; Brattleboro Daily Reformer 1921-09-21 p1; #102 photograph Oct 1937; Official Guide Feb 1952 (gone-by only). Headway is an unsourced estimate.

NO straight-line legs: 2.9 mi follows active NS track tagged old_railway_operator=Chesapeake Western out of Harrisonburg toward Pleasant Hill, and 4.23 mi follows the OSM railway=abandoned grade way (tagged old_railway_operator=Chesapeake Western) through Dayton to Bridgewater; that grade way is a long, lightly noded mapper's line and its curves are only as good as the mapping. segments.note: Bridgewater was the original western terminus: the 1896 public timetable runs Bridgewater - Elkton, 27 miles, 2 trains each way (headway_min 480 is an estimate from that count). Through trains Elkton - Bridgewater 1896-1902, thereafter through to Stokesville. Same opening-date conflict as Elkton - Harrisonburg (23 Mar vs late Apr 1896). Train counts 1897-1903 not checked.
sources: Segment-level: Staunton Vindicator 1896-05-15 p2 (schedule eff. 29 Apr 1896, Bridgewater - Elkton); Richmond Times 1896-04-28 p5. Headway estimated.

segments.note: Staunton Spectator timetables 1902-1911 run Harrisonburg - Pleasant Hill - Dayton - Bridgewater in the through Elkton - Stokesville / North River Gap service, 3 trains each way 1904-1911 (headway_min 360 is an estimate from that count). The 1921 discontinuance story describes a road 'running from Elkton to Stokesville', which strongly implies trains still reached Bridgewater in 1921, but no 1921 source names a station here, so it is not drawn. The Feb 1952 Guide's Bridgewater Branch table reads 'Operates for Freight, Mail and Express only'. Freight afterlife (context only): N&W abandoned Pleasant Hill - Bridgewater in 1987. [OPEN] 1911 is the last CONFIRMED year of passenger service on this stretch, not a known end - no source dates when passenger trains actually stopped here. Do not extend without evidence. The end bracket is 1911-1951.
sources: Segment-level: Staunton Spectator timetables 1902-10-03 p4, 1904-06-10 p4, 1907-07-12 p4, 1908-09-11 p1, 1910-01-14 p4, 1911-03-10 p1; Official Guide Feb 1952 (gone-by only).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 12.75 mi Bridgewater to Stokesville, against a documented ~13 mi (Fowler mileposts 27.0 -> 40; american-rails '13-mile line'). NO straight-line legs. The whole stretch is lifted (Mt. Solon - Stokesville pulled up 1930, west of Bridgewater by 1933; a 1949 flood destroyed much of the grade): about 10.8 mi follows the OSM railway=abandoned grade way tagged old_railway_operator=Chesapeake Western, and about 1.9 mi near Stokesville follows residential roads that OSM tags railway=abandoned on the old grade (Chesapeake Lane, Old C and W Railroad Road, Stokesville Road) - LATER ALIGNMENT STAND-IN: those road curves are post-railway and only approximate the grade. The mapped grade way is long and lightly noded, so its curves are approximate. OpenHistoricalMap has no geometry here. Simplified Douglas-Peucker 8 m.

segments.note: Built by W.E.D. Stokes to open his Augusta County timber and tan-bark lands; Stokesville was a company town (sawmill closed 1909). Opened 1902: track ballasted spring 1902 (Staunton Spectator 9 May 1902), directors' special from Stokesville 4 Apr 1902, and by Oct 1902 the public timetable runs Stokesville - Mt. Solon - Mossy Creek - Bridgewater - Harrisonburg with a new passenger depot at Stokesville (Staunton Spectator 3 and 10 Oct 1902). Wikipedia's 'by 1901' is construction, not service. 1904-1911 timetables: 3 trains each way through to/from Elkton; headway_min 360 is an estimate from that count, carried back to 1902-1903 unchecked. A Washington Evening Star resort ad of 28 May 1916 (Stribling Springs) gives 'R.R. stations, Staunton and Stokesville' - positive but indirect, NOT drawn. Mt. Solon - Stokesville abandoned 1930, cut back to Bridgewater 1933 - that is the latest possible end, not a known passenger end. [OPEN] 1911 is the last CONFIRMED year of passenger service on this stretch, not a known end - no source dates when passenger trains actually stopped here. Do not extend without evidence. The end bracket is 1911-1930.
sources: Segment-level: Staunton Spectator 1902-04-04 p2, 1902-05-09 p3, 1902-10-03 p4, 1902-10-10 p4; timetables 1904-1911. Headway estimated.

NO straight-line legs: all of it follows Stokesville Road, a residential road OSM tags railway=abandoned / old_railway_operator=Chesapeake Western on the old grade - LATER ALIGNMENT STAND-IN, the road's curves only approximate the grade. The trace ends where that way ends, at the North River Gap; the terminal's exact site is not established, which likely accounts for the ~0.4 mi shortfall.

segments.note: Not in the Oct 1902 timetable (which starts at Stokesville); in every timetable seen from 19 Feb 1904 ('North River Gap Ar.', trains 'Lv N. River Gap' to Elkton). [OPEN] start: 1904 is the earliest CONFIRMED year, not a known opening. An Aug 1902 Highland Recorder note of trains 'occasionally run to Wooddell Springs' refers to a logging tramway north of Stokesville and is not public passenger service. headway_min 360 is an estimate from the 3-each-way through timetable. Abandoned with Mt. Solon - Stokesville by 1930. [OPEN] 1911 is the last CONFIRMED year of passenger service on this stretch, not a known end - no source dates when passenger trains actually stopped here. Do not extend without evidence.
